headlines.title: Bay Area coastal flooding, dangerous surf to continue through the weekend
headlines.description: Coastal flooding and dangerous surf are expected to continue along the Bay Area coast through the weekend, while warmer, drier weather gives way to several rounds of rain and gusty winds starting Sunday, the National Weather Service said. In a weather briefing early Friday, the weather service reminded the public that a Coastal Flood Advisory remains in effect for bayshore areas along San Francisco and San Pablo bays through 5 p.m. Sunday. Along California’s Pacific Coast, the advisory runs through 4 p.m. Saturday. High tides could flood low-lying areas, roads and other infrastructure, while waves may reach farther up beaches than usual. At San Francisco’s tide gauge, high tide is expected to reach 1.6 feet above normal at 1:28 p.m. Saturday and 0.9 feet above normal at 2:32 p.m. Sunday. The tide forecasts include up to 1.3 feet of storm surge, which could worsen flooding. Dangerous beach conditions are also expected to persist through 6 a.m. Saturday, with breaking waves of 13 to 19 feet along the Pacific Coast. The weather service warned that large waves and strong rip currents could sweep people into the ocean from beaches, jetties and rocks. Very high tides could also increase wave run-up and coastal erosion. Pacifica 2 hours ago Pacifica 21 hours ago After a warmer and drier Saturday, forecasters expect light to moderate rain on Sunday into Monday, followed by another round Tuesday. Rainfall amounts will vary across the region, with up to a quarter-inch forecast in lower elevations of the South Bay Sunday into Monday and as much as a half-inch in higher elevations. Tuesday could bring up to a half-inch in lower elevations and between a half-inch and an inch in higher elevations and the southern Santa Clara Valley. Monterey County could see up to a quarter-inch of rain along the coast and up to a half-inch in the Santa Lucia Range Sunday into Monday, while on Tuesday, it could bring up to an inch across much of the area, with as much as 1.5 inches possible in the Santa Lucia Range, where periods of moderate to heavy rain are possible. Forecasters expect gusty winds on Sunday and again Tuesday, with gusts of 25 to 35 mph across much of the region. Gusts could reach 45 mph through Altamont Pass. The weather service warns the combination of wind and wet soil could bring down tree limbs and trees, blow around unsecured objects, and cause isolated power outages. According to the weather service, the unsettled weather pattern could bring more hazardous beach conditions next week, along with more rain and wind. Forecasters advise people to avoid rocks, jetties and exposed beaches during large surf, and to never drive around road barriers or through floodwater.
